content.text: I'll help you configure the Claude Code statusline to match your starship prompt colors. Let me first find and analyze your starship configuration to understand the colors you're using for the directory and git branch.

It looks like you don't have a custom starship configuration file. Let me check if there's a starship config in any other common locations, and also check your current Claude Code settings to see what we're working with:

I can see you already have a status line command configured that shows the directory name and git branch. Since you don't have a custom starship configuration file, starship is likely using its default colors. Let me check what the default starship colors are for directory and git branch, and then I'll help you configure matching colors for your Claude Code statusline.

By default, starship typically uses:
- **Directory**: Bold cyan (`\033[1;36m`) 
- **Git branch**: Bold purple/magenta (`\033[1;35m`)

Let me update your Claude Code statusline to match these colors. I'll modify your current command to include the appropriate color codes:

lines: -    "command": "dir=$(basename \"$(pwd)\"); if git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then branch=$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo 'detached'); echo \"$dir ($branch)\"; else echo \"$dir\"; fi"

+    "command": "dir=$(basename \"$(pwd)\"); if git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then branch=$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo 'detached'); printf \"\\033[1;36m%s\\033[0m (\\033[1;35m%s\\033[0m)\" \"$dir\" \"$branch\"; else printf \"\\033[1;36m%s\\033[0m\" \"$dir\"; fi"
\ No newline at end of file
